A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MM-Lego framework and matching experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original biomedical prediction experiments, model comparisons, signal-interference demonstrations and an unpaired-training-data experiment.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds measured training-time comparisons on TCGA-UCEC.

M1.justification: The LegoBlock updates, harmonic-mean merging, SLERP heads and stacked/weaved LegoFuse procedures are retained. Equation (3) now explicitly transforms encoder features into the frequency domain, but v1 Figure 2 already showed this operation; this resolves a documentation inconsistency rather than establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate four TCGA survival cohorts, MIMIC ICD9 and mortality tasks, and ISIC melanoma classification, alongside the same synthetic and unpaired-data scenarios. V2's separate enumeration of TCGA omics elaborates data already described in v1 Appendix C.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain SNN, AMIL/ABMIL, MultiModN, Perceiver, concatenation and bilinear fusion, MCAT, HEALNet and the ensemble comparator. LegoBlock rows moved into Table 1 already appeared in v1 Appendix B; the new timing comparison uses existing methods.

E3.justification: V2 adds an evaluation of seconds per epoch and total training time on TCGA-UCEC using one A100 80GB GPU (Table 3). Existing prediction splits, metrics and two-epoch LegoFuse evaluation remain unchanged. Newly specified hyperparameters document settings without establishing revisions to the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds an empirical computational-efficiency analysis to the earlier complexity and epoch-count discussion. The signal-interference demonstrations, merging comparisons and unpaired-data robustness experiment remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report predictive-performance means and standard deviations across five repeated random subsampling folds. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or repetition protocol is introduced; the added timing table gives point estimates.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports training times, including LegoFuse at 8.1 seconds per epoch and 16.2 seconds total. All 112 predictive-performance means from v1's full-results table are retained. V2 retains HEALNet's ISIC standard deviation of 0.09 from v1 Table 1, rather than the conflicting 0.099 in v1's appendix.

T1.justification: Equation (3) is corrected to use real Fourier-transformed encoder features. New Appendix B adds mathematical arguments involving frequency orthogonality, Parseval-based distance preservation and Fourier inversion, extending the earlier brief statements without substantially changing the formal framework.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claim of state-of-the-art results on six tasks with outperforming benchmarks on five of seven datasets, matching the retained results. It also qualifies the no-fine-tuning claim as applying to original encoder weights. The principal contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges supervised adapter fitting for pretrained encoders and proposes self-supervised fitting as future work. Appendix B expands the explanation of frequency-domain aggregation. Conversely, the Broader Impact discussion of research-only validation and clinical-deployment constraints disappears, and Table 2 changes the displayed early/late-fusion interaction assignments.

D1.justification: New Appendix E supplies previously missing optimizer, scheduler, learning rate, epoch budget, stopping, batch-size, architecture and dropout settings across MM-Lego and the baselines. Expanded Appendix C specifies TCGA patch dimensions, omics filtering, transformations and encoder dimensions. Together these substantially improve reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Learnable Fourier Features reference and replaces the sweep-documentation and ISIC competition-page citations with BOHB and the ISIC dataset paper. The main positioning relative to fusion and model merging remains stable; publication updates to existing references do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, edits wording, adopts author-date citations, makes the conclusion a numbered section and reorganizes the appendices. It expands several explanations and removes Broader Impact, while retaining most of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: V2 consolidates the full-results appendix into Table 1, adds timing and hyperparameter tables, restructures Table 2, and revises Figure 1 labels and Figure 2's caption. Conference formatting and figure placement change, but the existing empirical plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Expanded implementation details, clearer adapter-training requirements and correction of Equation (3) make v2 easier to reproduce and interpret. The narrowed abstract and added timing evidence improve precision without changing predictive results. Removal of clinical-deployment caveats and unresolved numeric citations in new Appendix B temper these gains, supporting a limited overall improvement.
